questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Press the brake and hold it down.
Grip the steering wheel tightly and brake gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel tightly and brake gently.
questions.explanation: When a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Slow down by easing off the gas and braking gently. Avoid stopping on the road. Instead, pull off safely to the side.

questions.question: When dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should slow down and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever visibility is poor. This helps other drivers see you as well.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are traveling in the wrong direction.
You must treat this intersection like a stop sign.
You cannot go until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must treat this intersection like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not yet entered it. You should:

options.text: Speed up to go through before the light turns red.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady yellow light before entering an intersection, stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light changes from green to yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: Which statement is false?

options.text: As weight increases, more alcohol is needed to raise blood alcohol content.
Between two people of the same weight, the person with more body fat will show signs of intoxication sooner.
Drinking three drinks in one hour affects you the same way as drinking three drinks over three hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking three drinks in one hour affects you the same way as drinking three drinks over three hours.
questions.explanation: Drinking faster causes higher intoxication. Three drinks in one hour affects you more than the same three drinks spread over three hours. Heavier people need more alcohol to raise their blood alcohol level. Among two people of the same weight, the person with more body fat will feel intoxication first because their body has less water to dilute the alcohol.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Move to the far-right lane immediately and speed up to match traffic.
Use the highway shoulder to reach traffic speed.
Speed up only after finding a gap in traffic, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after finding a gap in traffic, then enter.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic before speeding up to merge. Stay stopped while you wait for the right moment to enter safely.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross the centerline to pass on the left when it is safe.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you too closely, take your foot off the gas. This creates space between you and the other car without forcing you to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: Your wheels have run off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back on the road.
Grip the steering wheel, release the gas, and brake gently.
Brake hard and turn the wheels sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel, release the gas, and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, grip the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and brake gently. Once you slow down, check traffic and find a safe place to return to the road. Jerking the wheel sharply can cause you to lose control or hit other traffic.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout:

options.text: Brake gently.
Pump the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently.
questions.explanation: When a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Slow down by easing off the gas and braking gently.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: This five-sided sign warns you that you are near or entering a school zone. Watch for children and obey the speed limit.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely on a two-lane road, what should you do?

options.text: Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the other driver to pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.
Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the other driver to pass you.
questions.explanation: If another driver is tailgating you, try to change lanes if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed. This will encourage the tailgater to pass you.

questions.question: If you change your address, how long do you have to notify the Department of Safety?

options.text: Six months
10 days
45 days

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 days
questions.explanation: You must notify the Department of Safety within 10 days if your address changes.

questions.question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
Slow down, move to the right as far as possible, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right as far as possible, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: When you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down immediately. Move as far right as possible and stop off the road. Check if it is safe before continuing. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or be dangerous.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a road with no curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, the car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for bicycles, animals, or pedestrians that may cross the road.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Do not use the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Braking can make the skid worse.

questions.question: When parallel parking while facing downhill, how should you position your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or edge. When parking uphill without a curb, turn toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn away from the curb.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and a siren is approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or siren is approaching while you are in an intersection, finish crossing and then drive to the right and stop. Always yield to emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.
Proceed carefully without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the marked line and proceed only when it is safe. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk or intersection.

questions.question: Highway pavement is most slippery:

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain first starts.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first starts.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first starts. Dirt and oil on the road mix with the rainwater and create a slick surface.

questions.question: In rainy weather, be most careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed off the pavement and creates a slippery mixture with rainwater.

questions.question: If you are not in the proper lane to turn at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Signal and wait for a gap to turn.
Stop and wait until the way is clear before turning.
Drive to the next intersection to make the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection to make the turn.
questions.explanation: Never turn from the wrong lane. Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane. Circle back if needed.

questions.question: After a reportable accident, you must file a report with the Department of Safety and Homeland Security within:

options.text: 10 days.
20 days.
48 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: 20 days.
questions.explanation: The driver and/or owner of any vehicle involved in a reportable accident in Tennessee must file a report with the Department of Safety and Homeland Security within 20 days.

questions.question: There are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right. You should steer:

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
Between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When squeezed between oncoming and parked vehicles, steer a middle course between them.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more hazardous because you cannot see as well. Increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead to prevent a collision if the other vehicle stops suddenly.

questions.question: If your view at an intersection is blocked, you should:

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Maintain your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.
questions.explanation: Come to a complete stop at the intersection. Move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions before proceeding.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should turn into:

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: When turning, go from your lane into the first available legal lane in your new direction.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, adjust your speed to match traffic, signal, and:

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to completely clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap, adjust your speed to match traffic, and signal. Merge into the gap when safe. Do not expect other drivers to make room for you.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: You are following a small passenger vehicle.
Another driver is tailgating you.
You are driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or merge into another lane to prevent a collision. Do not brake suddenly.
